transcript.text: Alright, let's get started. We need to finalize the managed event-streaming service decision for the audit-event pipeline, since production integration is coming up next month. The current draft recommends NimbusMQ based on the lower initial quote and existing SDK integration, and staging showed both NimbusMQ and StreamForge handling 20,000 events per second without errors. Before I make the binding decision, I want to hear from backend engineering and procurement as part of the architecture review. I also want to flag that this pipeline will process events from customers in both North America and the EU, so we need to consider data residency and compliance implications. Who wants to kick things off?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: This morning I was helping another team investigate a load-test harness, and I confirmed that the production burst requirement for the audit-event pipeline is 40,000 events per second. The architecture document must specify required capacity as 40,000 events per second. NimbusMQ throttles at 25,000 events per second, while StreamForge supports 40,000. I haven't updated the architecture document yet because the harness investigation was a separate task, but this directly impacts the service selection — NimbusMQ would not meet the production burst requirement.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical procurement issue. I received the latest data-processing terms from our legal review just an hour ago: EU customer audit events must be stored in the eu-west-1 region, and only StreamForge offers the required eu-west-1 region under the shortlisted contracts. The StreamForge agreement needs a data-residency review commitment. I have not yet attached these terms to the architecture review, so this hasn't been visible to the rest of the team until now.
